headline: Staehr first winner on new marathon course
snippet: More than 300 participants took to the Wimmera River trails in Horsham on Sunday September 13 as part of the second annual Horsham Running Festival. Residents and intrastate and interstate travellers competed in the marathon, half marathon, quarter marathon or 5km event, with youngsters competing in the 2km dash. Event organiser Brian Haddy said it was good to have runners of various abilities take to the occasion, acknowledging numerous milestones, including marathon winner David Staehr from Kaniva. "David won it for the second successive year and has won the last nine events my company, Marathon Adventures, has run," Haddy said. "That was his 94th marathon and he's aiming to complete 100 marathons before he turns 50 next year. "One of our marathon pacers, Bryan Lypp, ran his 50th marathon of the year on Sunday, which is extraordinary. "At the other end of the spectrum, we had runners doing their first event or trying a new distance for the first time. "A woman was incredibly nervous at the start of her event but she was so delighted at the finish." Staehr finished the marathon in 2 hours, 47 minutes and 14 seconds, while Louisa Maney was the first female finisher in a time of 3 hours, 57 minutes and 12 seconds. In the half marathon, Tim Davis was the first finisher in 1 hour, 21 minutes and 54 seconds, while Kim Parker was the first female over the line in 1 hour, 44 minutes and 19 seconds. Haddy said the festival would retain this year's changed course, with the event set to count as an official marathon going forward. "We had a new course this year because the Weir Park Boardwalk we used last year was threatening to be either underwater or slippery," he said. "This year you would pass people running the other way for part of the loop, which gave it a bit more of a community feel. "We're going to stick to that course now because we've had it measured by the Association of International Marathons and Distance Races. "So for next year and beyond we'll keep the same course as it means if you run a fast time on that course it will count as a qualifying time for international marathons like Boston and New York." Haddy said going forward he would include the Horsham Running Festival as part of the Western Victoria Marathon Triseries, along with the Dimbooal Dash and Mildura Riverfront Marathon Festival. "Hopefully that will encourage more people to come to all of them and you get a special medal if do all three marathons next year," Haddy said. "Overall numbers were at about 330, which is a touch up from last year, but I think there's plenty of room for further improvement, which I think the triseries inclusion will help with." headline: GO says Melita’s proposed acquisition of Epic raises questions on competition and consumer choice
snippet: Telecommunications company GO said Thursday it is following the announcement of Melita's proposed acquisition of Epic "very closely". On Wednesday , Melita and Epic said they had reached an agreement to combine their operations, bringing together two of Malta's major telecommunications providers in a deal that remains subject to regulatory approval, the companies said in a statement on Wednesday. A statement by the two companies said that under the proposed transaction, Melita will acquire 100% of Epic from Monaco Telecom in the future. The combination and the companies' intended future investment remain subject to customary merger control and other regulatory approvals. The proposal, GO said Thursday, "raises important questions around competition, consumer choice, pricing, investment and innovation, particularly regarding the longer-term incentives to continue investing in networks and services. If approved, the transaction would reduce Malta's mobile network operators from three to two and significantly reshape the telecommunications landscape." As such, "we trust that the Malta Competition and Consumer Affairs Authority will undertake a rigorous, transparent, evidence-based and fully independent assessment of the proposed transaction and its potential impact across the relevant markets," GO said. Irrespective of the outcome, GO said remains focused on competing effectively and investing for the long term. Our commitment to Malta's digital infrastructure remains unchanged. We will continue investing in our nationwide fibre and mobile networks, developing our services and technology, and delivering strong value and service to all our customers.

headline: Google Gemini Notebook Gets a Major Upgrade: Here’s What’s New
snippet: Google announced new features for Gemini Notebook, the AI-powered research and study tool previously known as NotebookLM. The update introduces real-time voice conversations, an audio recorder and interactive learning tools such as quizzes and flashcards. The company is also offering eligible college students free access to its paid Google AI plans for one year, with higher usage limits in Gemini Notebook. Real-Time Voice Chats Gemini Notebook will soon let users have real-time spoken conversations with their notebooks through its mobile app on Android, iPhone, and iPad. Google says the feature will work in nearly 100 languages. Users will be able to ask questions, get step-by-step guidance and interrupt the conversation while speaking. Responses will remain grounded in the sources added to the notebook, letting users discuss study material through voice instead of typing questions and reading text responses. The feature is rolling out to Google AI Ultra subscribers aged 18 and above this week, with Google AI Pro subscribers and other users set to get access soon. Audio Recording Google is also adding an audio recorder to the Gemini Notebook mobile app starting next week. Users can record lectures, meetings or their own thoughts directly inside the app. The recordings will become sources in the relevant notebook, alongside documents, handwritten notes, worksheets and photos. Users can then chat with, cite and build from these recordings while continuing to edit their notes. Interactive Study Tools Gemini Notebook is adding interactive learning overviews under Reports, combining summaries with studio content such as infographics, quizzes and flashcards. New quiz formats will include short-answer, multiple-select and fill-in-the-blank questions. Users will also be able to review their quiz and flashcard performance through notebook chat and customise questions. Short Video Overviews are expanding to more than 80 languages, with videos of around 60 seconds combining narration and educational animations. Also Read: Google Gemini Notebook’s New Upgrade Could Change How You Study Free Google AI Pro for Students Eligible college students in the US can claim one year of Google AI Pro for free, normally priced at USD 19.99 per month. The offer provides 4x higher usage limits in Gemini Notebook. Eligible college students in more than 140 markets outside the US can receive Google AI Plus free for one year, with 2x higher usage limits. Both offers can be claimed until December 31, 2026, subject to Google's terms.
